articles.title: Darius Acuff Jr. Named Kings' Only Untouchable Player in New NBA Trade Rumors
articles.summary: The 2026-27 NBA season may just have tipped off, but the Sacramento Kings are already open to trading away nearly anyone on their roster.
articles.body:
The 2026-27 NBA season may just have tipped off, but the Sacramento Kings are already open to trading away nearly anyone on their roster.

Kings rookie point guard Darius Acuff Jr. is the only player the team is unwilling to discuss in trade negotiations, according to The Athletic's Sam Amick .

Acuff Jr. was selected with the No. 7 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft after he was named the SEC Player of the Year as a freshman at Arkansas. The 19-year-old has started his professional career on a historic pace, averaging 26.2 points, 7.3 assists and 3.8 rebounds through the first 11 games of his rookie campaign.

The impressive performances from Acuff Jr. has caused "internal excitement" that has the Kings "pondering ways to speed up their roster reconstruction," according to Amick.

Sacramento has plenty of excess weight on its salary cap. Kings center Domantas Sabonis and shooting guard Zach LaVine are both earning over $45 million this season, with Sabonis also accounting for $48.6 million next season, per Spotrac . Forward Keegan Murray is accounting for $24.1 million following the five-year, $140 million extension he signed last year, but he has been hampered by injuries since signing that deal.

The Kings are giving Acuff Jr. plenty of in-game experience early — the rookie is tied for second in field goal attempts per game (22.8) and leads all players with 37.4 minutes per game, per Basketball Reference .

articles.title: Yaxel Lendeborg Drops Candid Quote About Serving as Warriors' No. 1 Option After Steph Curry Injury
articles.summary: Yaxel Lendeborg has shown tremendous confidence already as a rookie, but he is also self-aware enough to know the pressure that comes with needing to be the No. 1 scoring option for the Golden State Warriors with Stephen Curry injured.
articles.body:
Yaxel Lendeborg has shown tremendous confidence already as a rookie, but he is also self-aware enough to know the pressure that comes with needing to be the No. 1 scoring option for the Golden State Warriors with Stephen Curry injured.

Speaking to reporters during Friday's shootaround, Lendeborg explained his confidence level is at a "six out of 10" believing he can fulfill Curry's big shoes and the remaining points have him wondering "am I going to be able to live up to it?"

Dray in Support of Yaxel's Trash Talk 🗣️

Curry is expected to miss around one month after the Warriors announced he suffered an oblique abdominal tear. The injury occurred in the first quarter of Golden State's 115-108 loss to the Houston Rockets on Wednesday.

This will be the first extended absence of the season for Curry. He previously sat out two games on Oct. 24 and Nov. 1 since they were on either end of a back-to-back.

Curry was having one of his best starts to a season in years before the injury. He averaged 30.6 points on 45.7 percent three-point shooting, 4.3 assists and 4.1 rebounds per game in his first nine games.

If there is a reason for Lendeborg to be confident, his numbers in the two games Curry missed suggest he is capable of handling a bigger role. He put up 26 points, nine rebounds and five assists against the Phoenix Suns on Oct. 24.

The Nov. 1 game against the Los Angeles Clippers saw Lendeborg set a career-high with 37 points on 13-of-19 shooting in 34 minutes. He also tied his career-high with six assists in the 124-112 win.

Friday night will be a much tougher test for Lendeborg than those previous two games because the Warriors are facing Victor Wembanyama and the San Antonio Spurs at Frost Bank Center.

Lendeborg entered the NBA as an older rookie at 24 years old. He has looked ready for every task that has come his way thus far, so there's no reason to think he will be intimidated by this moment.

articles.title: LaMelo Ball sure looks like the difference: Timberwolves and Hornets trending in opposite directions after trade
articles.summary: Minnesota is making moves in the West with LaMelo Ball, while Charlotte is stumbling in the East without him.
articles.body:
We will stipulate that, when it comes to success and struggle in the NBA, the answer is never just one thing. There's plenty that goes into teams' fortunes rising and falling, and all sorts of stuff can factor into the difference between living in the penthouse and taking up residence in the outhouse.

With that caveat in place: While the Minnesota Timberwolves were doing this in Minneapolis on Thursday, en route to dismantling the Dallas Mavericks, 133-94 …

… and the Charlotte Hornets were doing this in Phoenix on the same night, en route to a desultory 101-96 defeat …

… it was hard not to note the Just One Thing that seems to be contributing to the difference between Minnesota and Charlotte. Or, rather, the Guy Wearing No. 1.

After walloping a pretty good Mavs team, the Wolves are 9-3, in third place in the Western Conference, with the NBA's best net rating . They've won five in a row, and six out of eight since losing superstar No. 1 option Anthony Edwards to knee surgery . They've outscored their opponents by a total of 161 points this season; according to Justin Kubatko of Statitudes , that's the largest point differential through 12 games in Wolves franchise history — by 50 points .

After falling in Phoenix, mustering just 96 points against the league's fourth-worst defense , the Hornets are now 4-8, tied for 10th in the East, with the NBA's No. 26 net rating . They've lost seven of eight, have logged more turnovers than assists four times in 12 games , and have already failed to crack 100 points six times — as many times as Charlotte finished south of the century mark all of last season .

Again: It's not just that LaMelo Ball used to play for the Hornets, and now he plays for the Wolves. The operating theory for how Charlotte would generate offense in the absence of its one-time linchpin rested largely on continued growth and elevated production from Brandon Miller, Kon Knueppel and the re-signed Coby White, with a dash of second-unit contribution from veteran Dennis Schröder. The Hornets have gotten a grand total of 97 minutes thus far from White, who's on a minutes restriction as he works his way back from a left calf strain, and Knueppel, who'll miss the next several weeks with a balky left hamstring . Schröder's also on the shelf with a hamstring strain ; Miller, the team's leading scorer, has missed the last two games with a groin injury .

Any team would struggle to score without the bulk of its perimeter firepower, ball-handling and shot creation. It has to be painful, though, to be mired in such a horrific offensive morass mere months after consciously choosing to bid farewell to Ball, the player whom both the eye test and the advanced numbers suggested served as the rising tide that lifted Charlotte's offense last season.

And it must be particularly galling to be suffering through the doldrums while watching LaMelo have exactly the same kind of effusive, elevating effect in the Twin Cities.

Ball had nine of the Wolves' 33 assists in the blowout win over the Mavericks on Thursday — Minnesota's fourth 30-assist game of the season , more than anybody but the Hawks, Warriors, Nuggets and Spurs . Those helpers led to 19 Minnesota points, in addition to the 22 that Ball scored himself; for the season, he's directly creating 56.9 points of offense per 100 possessions for the Wolves, according to Databallr , which is 20th in the NBA — and nearly five points-per-100 more than White, who leads this season's Hornets.

The Wolves generate a higher share of their shots at the rim when LaMelo's on the floor than when he's off it. Their 3-point shooting goes through the roof in his minutes, and nearly every member of the team sees a bump in shot quality when playing alongside him .

The Wolves are more efficient in the half-court when Ball's at the controls, and they get out in transition way more often with him out there. Minnesota's team-wide effective field-goal percentage spikes by 6.5% with LaMelo on the floor — the largest on/off split on the team, and one of the largest among all NBA players to log at least 200 minutes this season, according to Cleaning the Glass .

The numbers tell a compelling story. So, too, does the joy that seems to leap off the screen from so many of the Wolves as they run with LaMelo — orbiting, emulating and ultimately benefiting from the irrepressible style and flow with which he plays.

"I think when you have a guy like Melo, he makes it fun for everybody," Timberwolves head coach Chris Finch said after Thursday's win, according to Sarah Todd of the Minnesota Star Tribune . "And the guys can trust in the next pass, next play."

That trust is tougher to come by these days in Charlotte, where the Hornets enter Friday's action ranked dead last in the NBA in points scored per possession , field-goal percentage , free-throw attempts , assists and turnovers , struggling to consistently string together quality possessions, even against lesser defensive outfits.

"How do we stop the bleeding?" White told reporters after a recent loss to the Detroit Pistons. "There's gonna be turnovers. There's gonna be miscommunications on both sides of the ball. How do we not let it continue to derail us from what we're trying to do?"

The loss of a superstar of Edwards' magnitude would've derailed plenty of teams. The Wolves, though, have continued to thrive, buoyed in part by the NBA's No. 1 defense — a unit on which Ball has somewhat surprisingly emerged as a physical and positive contributor at the point of attack. All told, Minnesota has outscored opponents by a whopping 15.5 points per 100 possessions when Ball has played without Edwards — a loftier net rating than even their regular-season leading mark, and more than good enough to stay afloat in the brutally competitive West while Ant continues to rehab his ailing knee.

There are plenty of other factors at play. The Hornets have underperformed their expected shot quality by more than any other team in the NBA thus far, according to Synergy Sports Technology's tracking; the combination of some regression to the mean and the hopefully healthy return of some key pieces should help bolster their offense. And there's plenty of credit to go around in Minnesota, from Rudy Gobert's perpetually stalwart work on the back line to Finch getting career-best play from the likes of Jonathan Kuminga, Ayo Dosunmu and Bones Hyland to a collective closing kick that has the Wolves ranked second in the NBA in fourth-quarter net rating .

"We've definitely [elevated] our play in the fourth quarters on both sides of the ball," Finch said . "Getting key stops, rebounding really well, executing, finding really good shots. And LaMelo's been at the heart of a lot of that on offense."

LaMelo's presence has been at the heart of a lot of what's gone well for the Wolves, and his absence, it seems, has been at the heart of a lot of what's haunting the Hornets. It's never just one thing. Sometimes, though, one thing can make one hell of a big difference.

articles.title: Dejounte Murray Trade Idea After New Orleans Pelicans Guard Requests Out
articles.summary: Dejounte Murray wants to be traded from the New Orleans Pelicans, according to ESPN's Shams Charania. This aligns with earlier reporting from Shamit Dua of In The N.O. that both player and team believed it was time to go their separate ways.
articles.body:
Dejounte Murray wants to be traded from the New Orleans Pelicans, according to ESPN's Shams Charania . This aligns with earlier reporting from Shamit Dua of In The N.O. that both player and team believed it was time to go their separate ways.

Now, the divorce process will accelerate.

As it just so happens, people inside the Phoenix Suns' locker room were reportedly annoyed that they don't have a real point guard on the roster . The team has already registered interest in Murray, per Chris Haynes of NBA TV .

Not sure about you, but it sounds like there's a deal to be made here.

In: Jalen Green, 2027 second-round pick, $3.5 million cash

As In The N.O.'s Shamit Dua writes, "many around the league believe the Pelicans and Murray would like to work together to find a better situation for the veteran guard." We can quibble over whether the Suns count as a "better situation." But landing on a team obsessed with playing past Apr. 11 makes at least slightly more sense.

Though Green isn't the cleanest fit in The Big Easy, he's nearly six years younger and more athletic than Murray. He also doesn't have an Achilles injury in his rearview. Last season was the first time he racked up a significant number of absences.

Despite identical career clips from beyond the arc, Green is the more dangerous shooter of the two. He moves differently when stationed away from the ball and ranked in the 64th percentile or higher of pull-up three-point efficiency during each of his first three seasons, according to BBall Index . Murray has cleared the latter threshold just once.

The Pelicans are burning most of their space beneath the luxury tax by taking on an additional $3.5 million salary. They'll get it back in the inevitable Jordan Poole buyout. Phoenix is also sending New Orleans the requisite cash to make up the difference. Extra seconds are always useful, too.

Most importantly, the Pelicans are opening additional runway for sophomore Jeremiah Fears. Few consider him lead-guard material, but head of basketball operations Joe Dumars is "extremely high" on him, according to Dua. New Orleans can now hand him the reins unchecked while also carving out extra on-ball usage for Zion Williamson and Derik Queen.

Out: Jalen Green, 2027 second-round pick, $3.5 million cash

Chris Haynes of NBA TV reports that " there's some growing frustration " in the Suns' locker room because the "roster does not have a point guard that could organize" the offense. If only Phoenix had a 2033 first-round pick to dangle in higher-end deals.

Murray isn't the perfect solution. His three-point efficiency has cratered since leaving Atlanta, and he's attempting his fewest triples per 36 minutes since he was a member of the San Antonio Spurs. That gets dicey for a Suns offense already light on shooting.

Capable ball-handling takes precedence anyway. Phoenix is too reliant on Devin Booker and Dillon Brooks for make-something-out-of-nothing plays. Collin Gillespie would already be starting if the Suns knew what they were doing, but he's not the spiffiest passer and gets targeted constantly on defense.

Acquiring Murray adds another layer of playmaking to the offensive ranks. He has routinely averaged more rim assists per 75 possessions than any ball-handler currently on the roster and has crafty enough live-dribble vision to optimize touches for Khaman Maluach. He remains a defensive upgrade over Green, too.

The Suns can balk at including the second-rounder and $3.5 million. Green is younger. But he's a wild card and a below-average passer. Murray has the higher baseline and could cost Phoenix noticeably less if his unlikely incentives don't cash.

Dan Favale is a National NBA Writer for Bleacher Report. Follow him on Bluesky ( @danfavale ), and subscribe to the Hardwood Knocks podcast, co-hosted by Bleacher Report's Grant Hughes .

articles.title: Warriors' Draymond Green Says Rockets 'Do Some Bulls--t,' Addresses Claim They're a 'Dirty' Team
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors forward Draymond Green doesn't believe that the Houston Rockets are a dirty team despite a recent on-court altercation between the two squads.
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors forward Draymond Green doesn't believe that the Houston Rockets are a dirty team despite a recent on-court altercation between the two squads.

"I don't get off into the dirty thing," Green said on Friday's episode of The Draymond Green Show (h/t HoopsHype ). "Every now and then you see some people that just do things that are down right dirty. And it happens and when it does, I'll speak on it. Do they do some bulls--t when we play them? Absolutely. I think the thing is that may irritate me the most is like they play super physical but then they start flopping sometimes, you know? So, I would say like that irritates me more, but I'm not going to sit here and call them dirty team."

During Houston's 115-108 win over Golden State on Wednesday, Rockets guard Marcus Smart was ejected after throwing a punch at Warriors center Charles Bassey.

Bassey called Smart's actions "dirty" after the game.

"He's been playing dirty the whole game, man," Bassey said, per Dalton Johnson of NBC Sports Bay Area. "I remember in the first half, I was trying to set a screen. Bro, he grabbed my knees. He was playing dirty."

Smart eventually received a three-game suspension from the NBA.

Houston has recorded 52 wins in each of the past two seasons largely due to its hard-nosed defense, ranking No. 6 in the league with a 112.1 defensive rating during its 2025-26 campaign (via NBA.com ).

This year, the Rockets' 109.3 defensive rating represents the seventh-best mark among all teams.

Green has similarly developed a reputation for his aggressive defensive approach that occasionally includes extracurricular activities, earning nine All-Defensive Team selections and one Defensive Player of the Year award during his tenure in Golden State.

He's also been ejected from 23 regular-season games throughout his career, the second-most in NBA history (h/t Mack Baltes of Warriors Wire).

The next meeting between the Rockets and Warriors will take place on Dec. 30.

articles.title: Un memorable Robinson lidera la épica remontada del Barça en el OAKA
articles.standfirst: Los culés iban 14 abajo, pero el base hizo 16 puntos en los últimos cinco minutos incluidos los 13 finales de su equipo y el triple ganador para tumbar al líder Panathinaikos
articles.summary: Los culés iban 14 abajo, pero el base hizo 16 puntos en los últimos cinco minutos incluidos los 13 finales de su equipo y el triple ganador para tumbar al líder Panathinaikos
articles.body: Un memorable sprint final de Justin Robinson le dio al Barcelona una heroica victoria en el OAKA ante el líder Panathinaikos (74-76). Ahora mismo, no hay un jugador más determinante en Europa en los instantes decisivos. Nadie como él para darle los balones calientes. Los azulgranas arrancaron el último cuarto 14 abajo (57-43), pero entre Tyrese Martin, con 12 puntos casi seguidos, y el base, que hizo 16 con cuatro triples en los últimos cinco minutos incluido el ganador a falta de cuatro segundos, obraron una remontada que congeló el pabellón ateniense. Quinto triunfo consecutivo para un conjunto culé que ha vuelto a demostrar que es irreductible. Porque se plantó en Atenas con cuatro bajas (Punter, Makoundou, Núñez y Evbuomwan), porque hasta el último cuarto tuvo una noche nefasta en el tiro, porque en el tercer cuarto estuvo cerca del naufragio, porque sufrió un arbitraje sibilino... Pero un día más se agarró al parqué y consiguió salir con vida. Cuando el Barça formaba su plantilla en verano, además de desconocidos para el gran público, estaba fichando a guerreros que nunca bajan los brazos. Minuto a minuto, fue resistiendo el Barça. Al final del primer cuarto, 17-17 tras un mal inicio. Al descanso, 33-32 después de verse siete abajo (31-24) y levantarse con dos triples de Parra y Robinson. Llevaban los culés 4/16 desde el arco. Ritmo lento. Poco acierto. Problemas de faltas de Parra y Brizuela, referente en los últimos partidos. Se echaba de menos a Punter y en el Panathinaikos aparecía ya Nunn (10 puntos y acabaría con 19). En el tercer cuarto, el Barça zozobró. Recibió un 7-0 para arrancar y la inspiración de Francisco (17), con dos triples, y los tiros libres estiraron la renta hasta una máxima de 57-43. Los culés metieron tres canastas en juego en ese periodo y perdieron seis balones. Cada ataque era una tortura ante la crecida física del Panathinaikos. Parcial de 24-11. ¿Remontar un partido así en el OAKA? Parecía imposible. No para este equipo. Martin, negado hasta entonces, encendió la mecha con nueve puntos casi seguidos. Luego añadiría un triple más para acercarse a 66-63. Sólo dos entradas de Nunn evitaban el colapso total de los locales, que no metían una de fuera. Un tapón colosal de Nebo a Yabusele echó más gasolina al fuego azulgrana. El partido estaba donde le gustan a Robinson. Con hielo en la sangre el base puso el empate a 66 y con dos tiros libres consumó la remontada. Respondió Francisco con un triple y replicó de nuevo el base azulgrana con otro. Hayes-Davis, que no había anotado en juego, desequilibró para el Panathinaikos con cinco puntos seguidos: 74-73 a falta de 19 segundos. La última tenía que ser para Robinson. ¿Quién sino él? A falta de cuatro segundos, se jugó un triple frontal ante la defensa de Bonga y el balón tocó la parte posterior del aro. En lugar de salir rebotado, cayó suavemente en la canasta. Era el punto 33 del Barça en el último cuarto, uno más de los que metió al descanso. Robinson metió los últimos 13 de este equipo tocado físicamente pero que jamás se rinde. Ni en el OAKA ni ante la pasarela de estrellas de Obradovic. 74 - Panathinaikos (17+16+24+17): Francisco (17), Badio (-), Bonga (4), Hernangómez (8), Mitoglou (2) -cinco inicial-, Sloukas (1), Hayes Davis (9), Grant (3), Nunn (19), Lessort (5) y Yabusele (6) 76 - Barça (17+15+11+33): Robinson (24), Umude (9), Martin (13), Parra (5), Nebo (5) -cinco inicial-, Gibson (-), Brizuela (4), Nkamhoua (7), Balcerowski (7) y Minaya (2), Árbitros: Mehdi Difallah, Damir Javor y Milivoje Jovcic. Eliminados: Parra (min.37) Incidencias: partido de la undécima jornada de la Euroliga disputado en el Telekom Center de Atenas.

articles.title: Zion Williamson's Trade Value Assessed by NBA Exec in Honest Quote Amid Pelicans' Struggles
articles.summary: The New Orleans Pelicans may have to give up on getting back a significant return for Zion Williamson should the franchise decide to dismantle the roster after Dejounte Murray's reported trade request.
articles.body:
The New Orleans Pelicans may have to give up on getting back a significant return for Zion Williamson should the franchise decide to dismantle the roster after Dejounte Murray's reported trade request .

"I was texting with an executive, asking about a potential Zion market," ESPN's Tim MacMahon said Friday on NBA Today (4:10 mark of the video below).

"He says, 'Can you trade Zion? Sure. Can you get a big return for him? No way.'"

Williamson has gotten off to an efficient start to the season so far, shooting 62.2 percent from the field while averaging 21.7 points, 5.2 rebounds, 2.6 assists and two steals while appearing in 11 of the Pelicans' last 12 games.

He called out his team by saying players and coaches needed to "look in the mirror" after conceding a blowout Wednesday loss to the visiting Brooklyn Nets.

Injury and conditioning issues have impacted Williamson throughout his eight-year career with the Pelicans, although last season he averaged 21 points while playing in 62 games. Pelicans head of basketball operations Joe Dumars said in September he considered Williamson to be "in impeccable condition."

Williamson met games played criteria to make his $42.2 million cap hit for this season fully guaranteed, per Spotrac . He has not yet guaranteed the $44.9 million 2027-28 cap hit remaining on his deal before he is scheduled to hit unrestricted free agency ahead of his age-28 season.

The Pelicans could potentially already have at least one landing spot to consider for Murray, who has been ruled out of Friday's NBA Cup action with a left ankle sprain.

NBA insider Chris Haynes reported the Phoenix Suns had "registered interest" in Murray shortly after The Athletic's Sam Amick reported the franchise is "motivated to swap [Jalen Green] for a proven point guard."

Charania had reported earlier on NBA Today the Pelicans and Murray's agent Rich Paul had been working "for the last several days" to resolve Murray's trade request.

It sounds like Murray is more likely to be immediately on the move than Williamson as the Pelicans look to regroup from a 4-8 start that has left the team sitting 12th in the Western Conference.

articles.title: Pelicans evaluating possibilities after trade request from Dejounte Murray, who recently rebutted criticism on social media
articles.summary: Murray is currently in his third season with the team.
articles.body:
The New Orleans Pelicans are evaluating potential trade opportunities for Dejounte Murray after a trade request from the All-Star guard, the team announced Friday .

The news comes the same week the 30-year-old Murray rebutted criticism on social media with since-deleted posts, one of which reportedly featured profanity. The Pelicans are 4-8 this season, including 1-8 in the games Murray has appeared in.

Murray won't play in Friday night's NBA Cup group-play game between New Orleans and the Memphis Grizzlies, the Pelicans announced, citing his left ankle sprain . His agent Rich Paul and Pelicans officials were reported by ESPN's Shams Charania to be working on a resolution earlier in the day.

The Phoenix Suns have expressed interest in the 2022 All-Star, according to NBA insider Chris Haynes.

The 2026-27 campaign is his third with the Pelicans, with whom he's currently averaging 13.4 points, 4.6 rebounds, 4.4 assists and 1.6 steals per game.

That said, Murray is shooting just 29.6% from 3, and he's committed four turnovers twice so far.

In the fallout of a 145-111 home loss to the 3-8 Brooklyn Nets, the X account for Pro Pels Talk, a Pelicans podcast, posted an array of game clips, breaking down the game film without mincing words. The commentary that accompanied some of those clips questioned Murray's on-court effort .

As reported by The Athletic , Murray responded to one of those posts, which showcased footage of him apparently misplacing a pass intended for forward Saddiq Bey. The ball ended up low and away, resulting in a turnover, whereas Bey seemed to be asking for it near chest level.

"Ohhhhh let's talk about it," Murray wrote back on X in a since-deleted post, per The Athletic. "When you run post plays, are they suppose to catch on the block or the 3pt line? Let's hear it Mr social media coach, Gm and President? You have no f***ing clue what we dealing with.

"Maybe you should ask the whole team individually how they feel on a serious note and then … rethink alot of s***."

Before that, Murray engaged with an NBACentral X post that noted how the Pelicans are 3-0 without him this season.

In a quote post, Murray used a slew of crying laughing emojis and then said this, as captured in a screenshot by a social media user :

"From what's going on INSIDE This sounds like someone hit you to say this!! THE 'SABOTAGE' IS REAL!!!!!!"

On Friday, he apparently reposted Charania's report about him wanting out of New Orleans. That repost no longer appears on his X feed, however.

Charania went on "NBA Today" Friday after breaking the news to flesh it out more:

"In the last several days, I'm told, Murray has met with the organization, has made it clear to them that he wants to go somewhere else and play a meaningful, key role on another team," Charania said on the program . "And we've seen Dejounte Murray, especially on social media, express his frustration with how things are going there. Clearly, it is not working out there. He is not going to be playing basketball in New Orleans for the time moving forward here."

"In the last several days, I'm told, Murray has met with the organization, has made it clear to them that he wants to go somewhere else and play a meaningful, key role on another team," Charania said on the program .

"And we've seen Dejounte Murray, especially on social media, express his frustration with how things are going there. Clearly, it is not working out there. He is not going to be playing basketball in New Orleans for the time moving forward here."

Charania noted that in Murray's absence, the Pelicans will turn over the lead guard position to 2025 No. 7 overall pick Jeremiah Fears. The 20-year-old Oklahoma product has averaged 18 points and nine assists in the three games Murray has missed this season.

Murray's been available for only 54 Pelicans games since he came aboard ahead of the 2024-25 campaign. He suffered a torn Achilles that season , and that injury kept him out of a good portion of last season, too .

Murray's best NBA season occurred in 2021-22, when he earned his All-Star recognition and led the league in steals during his final go-around with the San Antonio Spurs. He also spent two seasons with the Atlanta Hawks. They ultimately traded him to the Pelicans for two first-round picks, Dyson Daniels, Larry Nance Jr., E.J. Liddell and Cody Zeller.

articles.title: 'Physical as F--k,' JJ Redick Outlines Lakers' Identities After 'Audit' of 11-2 Start to NBA Season
articles.summary: JJ Redick says his coaching and analytics staff put together a 21-page "audit" detailing statistics that back up what he sees as the Los Angeles Lakers' identity after an 11-2 start to the season.
articles.body:
JJ Redick says his coaching and analytics staff put together a 21-page "audit" detailing statistics that back up what he sees as the Los Angeles Lakers' identity after an 11-2 start to the season.

Redick went over the audit with his team ahead of Sunday's game at the Phoenix Suns, he told reporters Friday (h/t ESPN's Dave McMenamin).

"We filtered through our offensive stuff based on our identities of who we want to be offensively: Organized, unselfish, advantage-based," Redick said. "And then we went to our defense, and our three identities: Organized, physical as f--k, and relentless."

Redick concluded, "We've done that for the last two and a half seasons. Everything that we present to the team lines up with who we're trying to be."

The Lakers are in the middle of a three-day break since their last game, a Wednesday victory at the Milwaukee Bucks that marked the team's seventh win in a row.

After taking on the 5-6 Suns this Sunday in Phoenix, the Lakers are scheduled for a four-game homestand against struggling teams in the 4-8 Charlotte Hornets and the one-win Utah Jazz and Sacramento Kings.

Redick will look to take advantage of that home stretch to further solidify his team's identity before the Lakers match up against the San Antonio Spurs later this month in what could be a battle for the top spot in the West.

articles.title: Montrezl Harrell Reveals He Nearly Fought Paul George During 2020 NBA Bubble, 'I Will Beat Your Ass'
articles.summary: Former NBA center Montrezl Harrell explained why he was almost involved in a fight with Los Angeles Clippers teammate Paul George during a second-round playoff clash with the Denver Nuggets in the 2020 NBA bubble.
articles.body:
Former NBA center Montrezl Harrell explained why he was almost involved in a fight with Los Angeles Clippers teammate Paul George during a second-round playoff clash with the Denver Nuggets in the 2020 NBA bubble.

During a Friday appearance on the Kowch Potatoes podcast, Harrell revealed that the disagreement stemmed from a miscommunication on defense while guarding Nuggets star Nikola Jokić.

"Bruh tried to start talking to me crazy and then tried to address me like, 'Bro, who you talking to?' Once he said that, all the basketball went out the window," Harrell said (0:57 mark). "I didn't think about nothing else. Lou had to grab me, Pat came up and grabbed me."

"I said, 'Bro, I will beat your ass. F--k all the basketball s--t, I will knock you the f--k out bruh. I'm not even playing with you.' I just started letting him have it," he added.

The high tensions between Harrell and George don't come as a complete shock, as reports from the bubble in Sept. 2020 indicated that the two players didn't see eye-to-eye.

Still, the Clippers were viewed as a top contender to capture a championship at the time with a rotation that featured George, Harrell, Kawhi Leonard, Lou Williams and Patrick Beverley.

Los Angeles compiled a 44-20 record to start its 2019-20 campaign before the NBA moved to the bubble in Orlando amid the COVID-19 pandemic.

The Clippers took down the Dallas Mavericks in the first round of the playoffs that year, but ended up blowing a 3-1 series lead over the Nuggets in the second round before they were eliminated.

George struggled against Denver, shooting just 38.2 percent from the field and 33.3 percent from behind the arc across the final three games of the series.

Harrell averaged 11.7 points and 2.6 rebounds per game while connecting on 54.9 percent of his field goals in the second round.

He ultimately joined the Los Angeles Lakers during the ensuing offseason, while George remained with the Clippers for four more years before signing with the Philadelphia 76ers in 2024.

articles.title: Can the Boston Celtics emerge as championship contenders?
articles.summary: The Boston Celtics are 10-2 to start the season, but is talk of contention still too early?
articles.body:
When the Boston Celtics decided to trade away Jaylen Brown earlier this summer, fans were understandably concerned. After all, the duo of Brown and Jayson Tatum had led to an NBA Finals appearance in 2022 and a championship in 2024. Without Brown in the rotation, questions began to arise regarding the Celtics' ability to build another contending roster during Tatum's prime years.

A 10-2 start to the 2026-27 NBA season may have eased some of those concerns. Not only are the Celtics playing good basketball, but they're also embracing the smaller details that create winning habits later in the season. Boston is also playing a higher-pressure style of basketball, jumping from 23rd in opponent turnover percentage last season to eighth to begin this campaign. Joe Mazzulla's team looks to be versatile on offense and relentless on defense.

With this in mind, NBC Sports Boston's Chris Forsberg and Kayla Burton recently discussed the Celtics chances of emerging as a genuine championship contender this season. The analysts pointed toward Boston's hot start to the season, the improvements in style of play, and the All-NBA level of production from Jayson Tatum as potential factors in a championship push.
